restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5: the compression works on register-resident words (H0..H7 chaining, W0..W15 block), one 32-step COMP32 call on them costs 1 unit, and every other primitive costs 1/2224 units, with jumps, moves, immediate register writes and the call issue each charged as one operation.
Complete fixed-IV SHA-256 with steps 0 through 31, standard message expansion, feed-forward, FIPS 180-4 padding and all 256 digest bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = BE32(x).

Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search run on one processor: theta = 2^-32, maximum chain length 2^40, evaluation budget K0 = 65162*2^112, record cap 2^98, main loop unrolled 16 times with a DP test after every evaluation, one run with no restart.

Time, memory and preprocessing are worst-case bounds for every run (time at most 2^128.00928, rounded up to 128.01). The success probability of at least 0.39 (bounded below by 0.3900080 under H-RF) holds under the declared random-function heuristic H-RF.
Generic attack with no cryptanalytic improvement claimed; no stored collision, advice or precomputation.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA-256-r32(BE32(x)) on 256-bit words x (digest read as a big-endian 256-bit integer): whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point it has not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value observed so far. This is the standard premise of the van Oorschot-Wiener analysis. It is used only to lower-bound the success probability (Section 6). Output correctness (Section 5) and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds (Sections 4, 7 and 8) are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: The fixed-IV 32-step SHA-256 restricted to 32-byte messages, iterated along pseudo-random chains from uniformly random 256-bit starts. The analysis uses only the chains started before the first contact (expected number at most 1 + K0*2^-32 + K0*2^-40 < 2^96; at most 2^98 + 2^88 + 1 chains in any run) and at most K0 - 1 + 2^40 < 2^128 main-loop evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: We ran the Section 4 algorithm (with n-bit starts, a hash map in place of the trie and no record cap) on output-truncated versions of the real 32-step map (n = 24, 32, 40 and 48 bits) and compared it with a keyed full 64-step control. These tests are extrapolated to the full 256-bit map. The analytic success bound itself uses only the H-RF statement, not the measured numbers.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is false as a literal statement about a fixed deterministic function; it is a heuristic model. The supporting experiments are our own and are not organizer-executed (no experiment manifest is declared); their full source and exact arguments are in the proof so every row can be regenerated. They cover only output widths of 24-48 bits on n-bit input subsets and cannot exclude a structural property that appears only at full width. The success bound exceeds 0.39 by only 8.0e-6; if H-RF overstated the contact probability by a small delta, restoring 0.39 would add about 2.4*delta bits to the scalar.
